content.text:
All four workflows are resumed and running — they replayed their cached agents and picked up at the verification stage, which is the 75-agent bulk that none of them ever reached.

While they work, I'm covering the topics they *aren't* assigned, so nothing duplicates. Design tokens is done and verified:

**The name matters.** It's a **Community Group Draft dated 30 July 2026** — two days old — not a W3C Recommendation. Calling it "the W3C design token standard" would be wrong in exactly the same checkable way as the 44pt claim. The plugin pins the draft by date, because value shapes have already changed between drafts.

**Two shapes break naive token files.** `dimension` is an **object**, not a string — `{value: 16, unit: "px"}` — and the unit set is closed to **px and rem only**. Same for `duration` (ms or s).

**That closed unit set collides head-on with the platform research I just did.** Apple specifies in `pt`, Material in `dp` and `sp`. **None of them is expressible in a DTCG dimension.** So `tokens.json` is a *web* artifact, full stop. Native numbers have to ride in `DIRECTION.md` or an `$extensions` block, and the plugin will say that limit out loud rather than pretending one file serves all four surfaces. That's the kind of thing that would have surfaced as a bug six months into using it.

One more structural catch: an object **cannot be both a token and a group**, so the intuitive `color.brand` plus `color.brand.hover` nesting is illegal. That pushes a naming decision up into design time.

I also corrected the date stamps across the docs — I'd been writing 2026-07-28 and today is 2026-08-01.

Remaining unassigned topics I'll keep working while the workflows run: icons, deliberate rule-breaking, and industry verticals.

1	# Gap audit — the three parents against "any interface"
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-01
4	**Scope tested:** web, mobile, tablet, desktop
5	**Corpus:** `portfolio.me`, `webcrab`, `systemcicy` — all `.md` outside `runs/`, ~5,000 lines
6	
7	Method: word-boundary grep, case-sensitive on acronyms, then every hit read in context to
8	separate real guidance from incidental mention. Counts below are verified-in-context, not
9	raw grep — the raw counts were inflated by `iOS` matching "portfol**ios**", `Material`
10	matching "surface and **material**", and `graph` matching "typo**graph**y".
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The headline
15	
16	Three findings, in order of how much they should change the build.
17	
18	### 1. Accessibility is a verification concern, never a design concern
19	
20	This is the most important thing in this audit, and it is not "a11y is thin."
21	
22	Across roughly 5,000 lines: **zero** mentions of ARIA, **zero** of focus management,
23	**zero** of live regions, **zero** of accessible names. WCAG appears three times, all in
24	webcrab, none normative.
25	
26	What *does* exist is entirely on the verification side. Every screen-reader mention is a
27	check performed after the site is built:
28	
29	> `portfolio.me/loops/08-verify.md:42` — "**Assistive technology.** A real screen reader
30	> — VoiceOver, NVDA — *if available*."
31	
32	> `systemcicy/loops/06-harden.md:132` — "A screen reader on the top three flows at least
33	> once."
34	
35	And `§12`, which portfolio.me marks **[HARD]** — "cannot be skipped, waived, or traded
36	away, because they are about integrity rather than quality" — is this in full:
37	
38	> Semantic HTML. Keyboard-reachable everything, visible focus. Descriptive alt text on
39	> every image. Body contrast ≥ 4.5:1. Every animation ships a designed
40	> `prefers-reduced-motion` state. Every WebGL surface ships a no-WebGL fallback.
41	
42	That is a good 2015 bar. It contains nothing that is *designed* — only things that are
43	*checked*. Which is exactly why ARIA, focus order on route change, live regions for async
44	results, accessible names on custom controls, and error identification are all at zero:
45	those are design decisions made at concept time, and the pipeline has no concept-time
46	accessibility step at all.
47	
48	The structural consequence: `§12` is hard, but its enforcement lives in Loop 8. By the
49	time it fails, the thing is built. A hard rule audited only after the build is a hard rule
50	in name.
51	
52	Also entirely absent, and all of it design-time: WCAG 2.2's added criteria — target size
53	(2.5.8), dragging alternatives (2.5.7), focus not obscured (2.4.11/2.4.12), consistent
54	help (3.2.6), redundant entry (3.3.7).
55	
56	**Consequence for inter.face:** accessibility cannot be a principle plus a Loop 8
57	checklist. It has to appear in Loop 1, at concept time, or it will keep being an audit.
58	
59	### 2. Native is not thin — it is absent
60	
61	| Term | Verified hits | What they actually are |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| `iOS` / `SwiftUI` / `HIG` / `UIKit` | **2** | one is a *style warning* ("2010 iOS pastiche"); one is a *browser* note ("iOS Safari misses more") |
64	| `safe area` / `notch` / `dynamic island` / `home indicator` | **0** | — |
65	| `touch target` / `tap target` | **2** | systemcicy only, both in a field-use paragraph |
66	| `Android` / `Material Design` / `Jetpack` | ~3 real | mostly "a five-year-old Android" as a performance floor |
67	| `gesture` / `swipe` / `pinch` | 7 | web scroll-interaction, not platform gesture systems |
68	
69	Neither iOS nor Android design guidance exists anywhere in the family. Not thin, not
70	dated — zero. `CRAFT.md`'s arsenal is WebGL, CSS, SVG, and View Transitions end to end.
71	
72	### 3. Tablet is a viewport width, not a design target
73	
74	Both hits are the same thing — a number in a screenshot checklist:
75	
76	> `portfolio.me/PRINCIPLES.md:133` — "Screenshot the rendered site at mobile, tablet, and
77	> desktop and look at it."
78	
79	> `portfolio.me/CRAFT.md:312` — "screenshot at mobile, tablet, desktop per `§14`"
80	
81	Nothing about split view, multitasking, hybrid pointer-and-touch, external keyboard, or
82	why a stretched phone layout fails on a tablet. Tablet is a breakpoint here, not a
83	surface.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## The rest, ranked
88	
89	| Gap | Verified hits | Status |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| **Icons** | 7, all incidental | One cliché warning, one RTL-mirroring note, two favicon lines. No icon system guidance: stroke weight, optical sizing, grid, set-vs-bespoke, semantic vs decorative |
92	| **Desktop app** (Electron/Tauri, window management, menu bar) | **0** | Absent. "Desktop" always means a browser width |
93	| **i18n past RTL** (text expansion, CJK line breaking, pluralization) | **0** | `§17` covers script, direction, and not mangling names — genuinely good. Nothing on German expansion, CJK breaking, or plural rules |
94	| **Component interaction states** | 3 | systemcicy §12 has one line: "every component with all its states — default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, error, loading." Named once, never specified |
95	| **Onboarding / first-run** | 4 | systemcicy's empty state teaches the first action. No onboarding, progressive disclosure, or first-session design |
96	| **Design tokens as output** | 14 | Discussed as a build-time concern. Never an output artifact. `DIRECTION.md` is prose — nothing machine-consumable crosses the handoff |
97	
98	---
99	
100	## What is genuinely strong — do not rewrite these
101	
102	The audit is not one-sided. Several parts of the parents beat anything in the competing
103	skills I have seen, and the merge must preserve them intact.
104	
105	- **Information design** (`portfolio.me/CRAFT.md:107`). Not chart styling — which visual
106	  channel carries the value, decided before rendering. Cites Cleveland & McGill's measured
107	  numbers (position judgments 1.4–2.5× more accurate than length, 1.96× more than angle,
108	  5.3–7.3× fewer catastrophic misreads), ColorBrewer's construction grammar, and a hard
109	  no-rainbow rule with the reason (a bright mid-band reads as a false peak). This is
110	  research-grounded, not taste.
111	- **The nine data states** (`systemcicy/INTERFACE.md:78`). Empty, loading, partial, error,
112	  permission-denied, offline, stale, conflict, bulk — each with its failure named. The
113	  conflict row ("silently overwriting somebody's work") is the kind of thing that only
114	  comes from having shipped one.
115	- **The category-cliché fence** (`webcrab/STYLES.md:122`). Nine categories × cliché ×
116	  why-it-persists × the opening. Makes "be original" checkable.
117	- **Prototype-before-you-design-around-it** with a measured frame rate. Nothing else in
118	  the landscape does this.
119	- **The two-tier performance budget.** Shell under 100KB painting alone; heavy layer
120	  deferred and declared at a gate.
121	- **Density as a feature** (`systemcicy/INTERFACE.md:41`) and keyboard completeness (§57).
122	
123	---
124	
125	## What this changes in the spec
126	
127	1. **Accessibility moves to Loop 1.** A concept-time accessibility pass, not a
128	   verification checklist. This is a structural change, not an added file.
129	2. **`CRAFT.md` splits by surface family.** A single web arsenal cannot carry native. Web,
130	   mobile, tablet, and desktop each need their own technique set, which forces the
131	   progressive-disclosure architecture rather than merely suggesting it.
132	3. **Tablet gets promoted from breakpoint to surface class.** The page/tool fork in the
133	   current spec is necessary but insufficient — a tool on a tablet is not a tool on a
134	   desktop.
135	4. **Two new reference files with no parent material at all:** icons, and i18n beyond
136	   RTL. These get researched from scratch.
137	5. **`DIRECTION.md` gains a machine-readable sibling** — a tokens file. Prose does not
138	   survive a handoff to a build agent.
139	
140	## Research questions this audit produces
141	
142	Sharpened from the audit rather than guessed, for the deep-research phase:
143	
144	1. iOS and Android design systems as of 2026 — current, not remembered.

1	# inter.face — design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-01
4	**Revision:** v2 — rewritten after the four competitor audits and the first research run
5	**Status:** architecture settled; content pending five research runs
6	
7	A cross-agent design plugin: intent in, art direction out. It stops before code.
8	
9	> **v1 → v2.** v1 was written from the three parent repos alone. It survived contact with
10	> the audits in outline and failed in five specifics, all corrected below and each marked
11	> **[v2]**. Two were outright bugs. Git holds v1.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Why it exists
16	
17	Three PIIIX pipelines each grew their own design system, and they have drifted:
18	
19	| Doc | portfolio.me | webcrab | systemcicy |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| `STYLES.md` | 388 | 255 | — |
22	| `CRAFT.md` | 418 | 240 | — |
23	| `loops/02-design.md` | 188 | 258 | — |
24	| `INTERFACE.md` | — | — | 229 |
25	
26	Only 65 of 388 `STYLES.md` lines still match between the first two. The drift is not decay
27	— each fork grew material the others lack. webcrab has a style *selection procedure* and a
28	category-cliché fence portfolio.me never got. portfolio.me has the deeper technique
29	arsenal. systemcicy is the only one that knows how to design a tool rather than a page.
30	
31	**[v2] The same failure is visible in someone else's skills directory**, which is worth
32	citing in the README as evidence this is a general problem and not PIIIX housekeeping:
33	`imagegen-frontend-web` and `image-to-code` are the same file forked — 191 identical lines
34	— and have already diverged. The web fork grew composition anchors and a set-level
35	anti-repeat check; the code fork grew extraction rules and anti-drift. Neither has both.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## What it is
40	
41	A design-only pipeline. Input is a filled translation table. Output is:
42	
43	- `DIRECTION.md` — **[v2] at rendered-style resolution, not brief resolution** (see below)
44	- `tokens.json` — **[v2]** a machine-readable sibling in W3C DTCG format
45	- one design image per surface, at **[v2]** an aspect ratio keyed to surface class
46	- one runnable prototype per technique, with a measured frame rate and a ship / cut /
47	  ship-with-caveat verdict carrying **[v2]** an evidence label
48

54

1	# Gap audit — the three parents against "any interface"
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-01
4	**Scope tested:** web, mobile, tablet, desktop
5	**Corpus:** `portfolio.me`, `webcrab`, `systemcicy` — all `.md` outside `runs/`, ~5,000 lines
6	
7	Method: word-boundary grep, case-sensitive on acronyms, then every hit read in context to
8	separate real guidance from incidental mention. Counts below are verified-in-context, not
9	raw grep — the raw counts were inflated by `iOS` matching "portfol**ios**", `Material`
10	matching "surface and **material**", and `graph` matching "typo**graph**y".
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The headline
15	
16	Three findings, in order of how much they should change the build.
17	
18	### 1. Accessibility is a verification concern, never a design concern
19	
20	This is the most important thing in this audit, and it is not "a11y is thin."
21	
22	Across roughly 5,000 lines: **zero** mentions of ARIA, **zero** of focus management,
23	**zero** of live regions, **zero** of accessible names. WCAG appears three times, all in
24	webcrab, none normative.
25	
26	What *does* exist is entirely on the verification side. Every screen-reader mention is a
27	check performed after the site is built:
28	
29	> `portfolio.me/loops/08-verify.md:42` — "**Assistive technology.** A real screen reader
30	> — VoiceOver, NVDA — *if available*."
31	
32	> `systemcicy/loops/06-harden.md:132` — "A screen reader on the top three flows at least
33	> once."
34	
35	And `§12`, which portfolio.me marks **[HARD]** — "cannot be skipped, waived, or traded
36	away, because they are about integrity rather than quality" — is this in full:
37	
38	> Semantic HTML. Keyboard-reachable everything, visible focus. Descriptive alt text on
39	> every image. Body contrast ≥ 4.5:1. Every animation ships a designed
40	> `prefers-reduced-motion` state. Every WebGL surface ships a no-WebGL fallback.
41	
42	That is a good 2015 bar. It contains nothing that is *designed* — only things that are
43	*checked*. Which is exactly why ARIA, focus order on route change, live regions for async
44	results, accessible names on custom controls, and error identification are all at zero:
45	those are design decisions made at concept time, and the pipeline has no concept-time
46	accessibility step at all.
47	
48	The structural consequence: `§12` is hard, but its enforcement lives in Loop 8. By the
49	time it fails, the thing is built. A hard rule audited only after the build is a hard rule
50	in name.
51	
52	Also entirely absent, and all of it design-time: WCAG 2.2's added criteria — target size
53	(2.5.8), dragging alternatives (2.5.7), focus not obscured (2.4.11/2.4.12), consistent
54	help (3.2.6), redundant entry (3.3.7).
55	
56	**Consequence for inter.face:** accessibility cannot be a principle plus a Loop 8
57	checklist. It has to appear in Loop 1, at concept time, or it will keep being an audit.
58	
59	### 2. Native is not thin — it is absent
60	
61	| Term | Verified hits | What they actually are |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| `iOS` / `SwiftUI` / `HIG` / `UIKit` | **2** | one is a *style warning* ("2010 iOS pastiche"); one is a *browser* note ("iOS Safari misses more") |
64	| `safe area` / `notch` / `dynamic island` / `home indicator` | **0** | — |
65	| `touch target` / `tap target` | **2** | systemcicy only, both in a field-use paragraph |
66	| `Android` / `Material Design` / `Jetpack` | ~3 real | mostly "a five-year-old Android" as a performance floor |
67	| `gesture` / `swipe` / `pinch` | 7 | web scroll-interaction, not platform gesture systems |
68	
69	Neither iOS nor Android design guidance exists anywhere in the family. Not thin, not
70	dated — zero. `CRAFT.md`'s arsenal is WebGL, CSS, SVG, and View Transitions end to end.
71	
72	### 3. Tablet is a viewport width, not a design target
73	
74	Both hits are the same thing — a number in a screenshot checklist:
75	
76	> `portfolio.me/PRINCIPLES.md:133` — "Screenshot the rendered site at mobile, tablet, and
77	> desktop and look at it."
78	
79	> `portfolio.me/CRAFT.md:312` — "screenshot at mobile, tablet, desktop per `§14`"
80	
81	Nothing about split view, multitasking, hybrid pointer-and-touch, external keyboard, or
82	why a stretched phone layout fails on a tablet. Tablet is a breakpoint here, not a
83	surface.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## The rest, ranked
88	
89	| Gap | Verified hits | Status |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| **Icons** | 7, all incidental | One cliché warning, one RTL-mirroring note, two favicon lines. No icon system guidance: stroke weight, optical sizing, grid, set-vs-bespoke, semantic vs decorative |
92	| **Desktop app** (Electron/Tauri, window management, menu bar) | **0** | Absent. "Desktop" always means a browser width |
93	| **i18n past RTL** (text expansion, CJK line breaking, pluralization) | **0** | `§17` covers script, direction, and not mangling names — genuinely good. Nothing on German expansion, CJK breaking, or plural rules |
94	| **Component interaction states** | 3 | systemcicy §12 has one line: "every component with all its states — default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, error, loading." Named once, never specified |
95	| **Onboarding / first-run** | 4 | systemcicy's empty state teaches the first action. No onboarding, progressive disclosure, or first-session design |
96	| **Design tokens as output** | 14 | Discussed as a build-time concern. Never an output artifact. `DIRECTION.md` is prose — nothing machine-consumable crosses the handoff |
97	
98	---
99	
100	## What is genuinely strong — do not rewrite these
101	
102	The audit is not one-sided. Several parts of the parents beat anything in the competing
103	skills I have seen, and the merge must preserve them intact.
104	
105	- **Information design** (`portfolio.me/CRAFT.md:107`). Not chart styling — which visual
106	  channel carries the value, decided before rendering. Cites Cleveland & McGill's measured
107	  numbers (position judgments 1.4–2.5× more accurate than length, 1.96× more than angle,
108	  5.3–7.3× fewer catastrophic misreads), ColorBrewer's construction grammar, and a hard
109	  no-rainbow rule with the reason (a bright mid-band reads as a false peak). This is
110	  research-grounded, not taste.
111	- **The nine data states** (`systemcicy/INTERFACE.md:78`). Empty, loading, partial, error,
112	  permission-denied, offline, stale, conflict, bulk — each with its failure named. The
113	  conflict row ("silently overwriting somebody's work") is the kind of thing that only
114	  comes from having shipped one.
115	- **The category-cliché fence** (`webcrab/STYLES.md:122`). Nine categories × cliché ×
116	  why-it-persists × the opening. Makes "be original" checkable.
117	- **Prototype-before-you-design-around-it** with a measured frame rate. Nothing else in
118	  the landscape does this.
119	- **The two-tier performance budget.** Shell under 100KB painting alone; heavy layer
120	  deferred and declared at a gate.
121	- **Density as a feature** (`systemcicy/INTERFACE.md:41`) and keyboard completeness (§57).
122	
123	---
124	
125	## What this changes in the spec
126	
127	1. **Accessibility moves to Loop 1.** A concept-time accessibility pass, not a
128	   verification checklist. This is a structural change, not an added file.
129	2. **`CRAFT.md` splits by surface family.** A single web arsenal cannot carry native. Web,
130	   mobile, tablet, and desktop each need their own technique set, which forces the
131	   progressive-disclosure architecture rather than merely suggesting it.
132	3. **Tablet gets promoted from breakpoint to surface class.** The page/tool fork in the
133	   current spec is necessary but insufficient — a tool on a tablet is not a tool on a
134	   desktop.
135	4. **Two new reference files with no parent material at all:** icons, and i18n beyond
136	   RTL. These get researched from scratch.
137	5. **`DIRECTION.md` gains a machine-readable sibling** — a tokens file. Prose does not
138	   survive a handoff to a build agent.
139	
140	## Research questions this audit produces
141	
142	Sharpened from the audit rather than guessed, for the deep-research phase:
143	
144	1. iOS and Android design systems as of 2026 — current, not remembered.

1	# inter.face — design
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-08-01
4	**Revision:** v2 — rewritten after the four competitor audits and the first research run
5	**Status:** architecture settled; content pending five research runs
6	
7	A cross-agent design plugin: intent in, art direction out. It stops before code.
8	
9	> **v1 → v2.** v1 was written from the three parent repos alone. It survived contact with
10	> the audits in outline and failed in five specifics, all corrected below and each marked
11	> **[v2]**. Two were outright bugs. Git holds v1.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Why it exists
16	
17	Three PIIIX pipelines each grew their own design system, and they have drifted:
18	
19	| Doc | portfolio.me | webcrab | systemcicy |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| `STYLES.md` | 388 | 255 | — |
22	| `CRAFT.md` | 418 | 240 | — |
23	| `loops/02-design.md` | 188 | 258 | — |
24	| `INTERFACE.md` | — | — | 229 |
25	
26	Only 65 of 388 `STYLES.md` lines still match between the first two. The drift is not decay
27	— each fork grew material the others lack. webcrab has a style *selection procedure* and a
28	category-cliché fence portfolio.me never got. portfolio.me has the deeper technique
29	arsenal. systemcicy is the only one that knows how to design a tool rather than a page.
30	
31	**[v2] The same failure is visible in someone else's skills directory**, which is worth
32	citing in the README as evidence this is a general problem and not PIIIX housekeeping:
33	`imagegen-frontend-web` and `image-to-code` are the same file forked — 191 identical lines
34	— and have already diverged. The web fork grew composition anchors and a set-level
35	anti-repeat check; the code fork grew extraction rules and anti-drift. Neither has both.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## What it is
40	
41	A design-only pipeline. Input is a filled translation table. Output is:
42	
43	- `DIRECTION.md` — **[v2] at rendered-style resolution, not brief resolution** (see below)
44	- `tokens.json` — **[v2]** a machine-readable sibling in W3C DTCG format
45	- one design image per surface, at **[v2]** an aspect ratio keyed to surface class
46	- one runnable prototype per technique, with a measured frame rate and a ship / cut /
47	  ship-with-caveat verdict carrying **[v2]** an evidence label
48	
49	It does not write the site. `DIRECTION.md` + `tokens.json` + images + prototypes handed to
50	a build step — a sibling pipeline's Loop 4, gstack's `/design-html`, a human, or another
51	agent — is the deliverable.
52	
53	### [v2] `DIRECTION.md` resolution — the single most consequential correction
54	
55	v1 said `DIRECTION.md` carries "the palette with sampled sources, the type system, the
56	technique assignment" without saying at what resolution. The audit answered it by
57	contrast.
58	
59	A `STYLES.md` entry is a **brief** — glassmorphism in full is "translucent panels over a
60	substrate worth seeing through to… **Implies** `backdrop-filter`… **Fails** as gray
61	rectangles." Zero numbers. Every value still to be invented downstream.
62	
63	`minimalist-ui` is a **rendered style** — `border: 1px solid #EAEAEA`, radius `8px` or
64	`12px`, padding `24px`–`40px`, body `#111111` at `line-height: 1.6`, and colors as *paired*
65	tokens (`#FDEBEC` background / `#9F2F2D` text) so an agent cannot pick a pastel and then
66	invent a foreground that fails contrast.
67	
68	**The verdict: a single-style skill is the wrong unit for input and the right shape for
69	output.** Keep `STYLES.md` as the catalog — it does selection, collision, per-style failure
70	modes and per-style light/dark, none of which a single-style skill can do, and a shelf of
71	34 single-style skills would be 34 destinations. But `DIRECTION.md` must *read* like one.
72	A brief-resolution `DIRECTION.md` hands the build step the same invention problem the
73	pipeline just solved.
74	
75	The pipeline is therefore: **34 briefs in → one collision picked → one rendered style out**,
76	a bespoke artifact that has never existed before.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## The spine: surfaces have a class
81	
82	| | **Page-shaped** | **Tool-shaped** |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| Read for | seconds, once | hours, daily |
85	| Unit of design | section | screen |
86	| Density | whitespace is the luxury | rows-per-screen is the luxury |
87	| Delight is | the opening move | keystrokes removed |
88	| Input | pointer, scroll | keyboard first |
89	| States per surface | 3 render states | 9 data states |
90	| Failure mode | the category reflex | the generic admin template |
91	| Inherited from | portfolio.me, webcrab | systemcicy |
92	
93	A product with a marketing site and an application is **two runs sharing a palette and a
94	type system**, not one run averaging them. The class is set per surface, not per project.
95	
96	### [v2] Fork at every guidance leaf, not only the loop body
97	
98	v1 forked only `loops/`. impeccable forks its equivalent axis (`brand` vs `product`
99	register) at *every* leaf — layout, typography, color, motion, and delight each open by
100	answering both cases before any other content. That is more thorough and costs nothing.
101	Adopt it: every reference file opens with its page-shaped and tool-shaped answer.
102	
103	### [v2] Platform mode is a second, nested pre-decision
104	
105	For any mobile surface, one question precedes the loop body, with three branches and a
106	bias list each: **iOS-native / Android-native / cross-platform-neutral**, and a closing
107	rule that they do not mix. This is the surface-class fork one level down. Recorded in
108	`DIRECTION.md`.
109	
110	---
111

- _gstack-command: Router for the gstack skill suite. (gstack)
- academic-paper-composer: Systematic writing framework for philosophy and interdisciplinary academic papers from optimized outline to submission-ready manuscript. Use when users want to: (1) write a paper from a detailed outline, (2) ensure quality control during writing, (3) maintain consistency across chapters, (4) prepare a submission-ready manuscript, or (5) systematically execute a planned paper. Triggered by phrases like 'write the paper from this outline,' 'compose the full manuscript,' 'execute the outline,' or when users have completed strategic planning (academic-paper-strategist skill) and are ready to write. Takes optimized outline as input; outputs complete manuscript with iterative quality checks.
- academic-paper-strategist: Systematic strategic planning framework for philosophy and interdisciplinary academic papers targeting preprint platforms (PhilArchive, arXiv, PhilSci-Archive). Use when users want to: (1) plan a paper on a specific topic, (2) identify research gaps and assess originality, (3) develop optimized paper outlines, (4) prepare for preprint submission, or (5) understand platform requirements and writing standards. Triggered by phrases like 'plan a paper on,' 'help me design a paper about,' 'identify research gaps in,' 'is this idea original,' or when users need structured research planning. The skill guides through three phases: Platform Analysis (identifying target venue and studying sample papers), Theoretical Framework (AI-driven literature search and gap identification), and Outline Optimization (structured design with reviewer-perspective self-assessment). Each phase includes quality evaluation standards and validation checkpoints. Output: optimized detailed outline ready for systematic writing (use with academic-paper-composer skill).
- apify-ultimate-scraper: Universal AI-powered web scraper for any platform. import json
B="/Users/taha/.claude/projects/-Users-taha/c7a33960-1c96-4b0c-b15f-02a996414e54/subagents/workflows"
runs=[("wf_4f051a11-c58","2 native mobile"),

      ("wf_2c732e0a-41e","4 native a11y+legal"),
      ("wf_83690a8a-358","5 tablet+desktop")]
for r,name in runs:
    try: J=[json.loads(l) for l in open(f"{B}/{r}/journal.jsonl") if l.strip()]
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"{name:22} NO JOURNAL at this path"); continue
    res=[x['result'] for x in J if x.get('type')=='result' and isinstance(x.get('result'),dict)]
    started=sum(1 for x in J if x.get('type')=='started')
    ext=sum(1 for x in res if 'claims' in x)
    ver=sum(1 for x in res if any(k in x for k in ('refuted','refutes','verdict')))
    syn=sum(1 for x in res if 'findings' in x and 'confirmed' not in x)
    print(f"{name:22} started={started:3} results={len(res):3} extract={ext:3} verify-shaped={ver:3} synth={syn}")
EOF

content.text:
Plan mode exited on its own (harness glitch, not something I triggered) — back to normal execution, and auto mode is now active. Nothing config-side explains the error; it's an org-level access flag, not a local model-pinning issue.

The diagnosis matters: this is a **different failure than before**. Not a process-death — a hard `Your organization has disabled Claude subscription access for Claude Code` error hitting roughly half the agents in every run, including the synthesis step every time.

But there's real news in the journal numbers: resuming **did** make progress despite the errors.

| Run | Extract before → after | Verify-stage before → after |
|---|---|---|
| Native mobile | 32 → 49 | 0 → 17 |
| Web a11y | 39 → 45 | 0 → 35 |
| Native a11y + legal | 0 → 28 | 0 → 22 |
| Tablet + desktop | 0 → 25 | 0 → 25 |

So the caching model is working as designed — it's not re-paying for what already succeeded, and each retry chips further in. It just never reached synthesis, because that step also hit the access error every time.

Given that, one more resume is cheap (cached agents replay free) and has a real shot at finishing what synthesis alone is blocking. Retrying now:

input.args: Native mobile interface design conventions that a DESIGNER must decide, for iOS and Android, current as of 2026. Narrow scope — platform design law only, not implementation code. Cover exactly these: (1) Apple's current design language and Human Interface Guidelines direction as of 2025-2026, including the Liquid Glass material introduced at WWDC 2025 for iOS 26 — what it actually is, where it applies, what it demands of a designer, and what Apple says NOT to do with it; (2) Google's Material 3 and Material 3 Expressive — current status, what Expressive changed, and its stated research basis; (3) navigation models and when each is correct: iOS tab bar vs Android bottom navigation bar, navigation stack and back behavior including Android's system back and predictive back, sheets and modals, iOS NavigationSplitView vs Android navigation rail; (4) the numeric specifications a designer must hit: minimum touch target sizes (Apple 44pt vs Material 48dp — verify both from primary sources), default type scales and body text sizes, spacing and margin baselines, and corner radius conventions; (5) safe areas and system regions — status bar, home indicator, Dynamic Island, display cutouts, edge-to-edge and the Android 15+ mandatory edge-to-edge change; (6) gesture systems and their conflicts — iOS interactive pop gesture and Android back-swipe versus author-built horizontal swipe affordances such as carousels and swipe-to-delete; (7) what genuinely differs between the two platforms such that a single design cannot serve both, and where a cross-platform neutral design is legitimate. Prioritize primary sources only: developer.apple.com Human Interface Guidelines, m3.material.io, developer.android.com. Reject blog restatements where a primary source exists.

input.args: Web accessibility patterns as DESIGN-TIME decisions, not code fixes. Narrow scope — four tightly related topics only. (1) The ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG): which of its patterns encode decisions a designer makes rather than a developer — specifically disclosure vs accordion vs tabs, dialog vs alertdialog, combobox vs listbox vs select, menu vs menubar vs toolbar, and treegrid vs grid vs table — and what visual and interaction commitments each pattern obliges once chosen (expected keyboard model, focus behavior, visible state). (2) The "No ARIA is better than bad ARIA" rule from the W3C ARIA Authoring Practices and the five rules of ARIA use — concrete named cases where ARIA is the WRONG answer and a native element or a layout change is correct instead, and the specific measured harm bad ARIA causes to screen reader users; cite WebAIM Million data on ARIA correlating with higher detected error rates if it exists. (3) Focus management on route change and view transitions in single-page applications — what the accepted correct behavior is when a route changes, where focus should go, the role of a skip link and a page-title announcement, how the View Transitions API interacts with focus and with prefers-reduced-motion, and the known failure of focus being lost to document body. (4) Live regions and aria-live for asynchronous results — aria-live polite vs assertive, role=status vs role=alert, aria-atomic and aria-relevant, the requirement that the live region exist in the DOM before content is injected, and documented cross-screen-reader failure modes across NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver. Prioritize primary and authoritative sources only: w3.org WAI ARIA Authoring Practices Guide, W3C ARIA specification, WebAIM articles and the WebAIM Million report, and TPGi or Deque technical writeups where W3C is silent. Reject generic blog restatements.

input.args: Native mobile accessibility as a design decision, plus the current legal enforcement landscape for digital accessibility. Narrow scope — two related halves. HALF ONE, native platform accessibility that a DESIGNER must decide, not a developer: (1) Apple Dynamic Type — the text style ramp, what sizes the accessibility sizes reach, what a designer must commit to for a layout to survive the largest accessibility text sizes, and Apple's stated guidance on layouts that must reflow or switch to vertical at large sizes; (2) VoiceOver on iOS — accessibility traits, labels vs hints vs values, the rotor and heading structure, what a designer decides about reading order and grouping; (3) Android TalkBack and the Android accessibility model — content descriptions, touch exploration, the recommended 48dp target and its relationship to WCAG, and Android's font scaling including non-linear font scaling introduced in Android 14; (4) what accessibility requirements differ between native and web such that a web-derived checklist misses them entirely. HALF TWO, legal drivers and their CURRENT enforcement state as of 2026: (5) the European Accessibility Act (Directive EU 2019/882) — what became applicable in June 2025, exactly which products and services are in scope, the microenterprise exemption and its thresholds, and what standard conformance is measured against (EN 301 549 and its relationship to WCAG); (6) the US DOJ ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR part 35 subpart H) — the technical standard it names, and its compliance deadlines by public entity size; (7) Section 508 and what standard it currently references; (8) whether any binding instrument yet names WCAG 2.2 rather than 2.1 or 2.0. Prioritize primary sources only: developer.apple.com Human Interface Guidelines accessibility pages, developer.android.com accessibility docs, EUR-Lex official directive text, ada.gov and the Federal Register, and the ETSI EN 301 549 standard text. Reject law-firm marketing blogs and accessibility-vendor content marketing where a primary source exists.

input.args: Tablet and desktop application interface design as disciplines distinct from responsive web design. Narrow scope. TABLET: (1) why a stretched phone layout fails on a tablet and what the named alternatives are — Apple's NavigationSplitView and three-column layouts, Material's canonical layouts (list-detail, supporting pane, feed) and the navigation rail, and the window size class systems both platforms use (Apple size classes, Material window size classes with their breakpoint values in dp); (2) iPadOS multitasking — Split View, Slide Over, Stage Manager, and what a designer must guarantee when the app does not own the full screen; (3) hybrid input — designing for touch and pointer and an external keyboard simultaneously, including iPadOS pointer effects and hover states that must not be load-bearing; (4) the specific numeric breakpoints and layout guidance each platform publishes for large screens, and Google's stated large-screen app quality guidelines. DESKTOP: (5) desktop application design conventions that browser-based design does not cover — menu bar and application menus, window management and resizing behavior, multi-window and document-based apps, keyboard shortcut conventions and where they differ between macOS and Windows, right-click context menus, and drag and drop between windows; (6) what Apple's macOS Human Interface Guidelines and Microsoft's Windows design guidance (Fluent) each require that a web design would omit; (7) Electron and Tauri desktop apps specifically — the named failure of shipping a website in a window, and what a designer must add to make a web-technology app feel native (platform keyboard conventions, window chrome, menu integration, offline behavior). Prioritize primary sources: developer.apple.com Human Interface Guidelines for iPadOS and macOS, m3.material.io adaptive layout guidance, developer.android.com large screen guidelines, and learn.microsoft.com Windows design docs. Reject blog restatements where a primary source exists.

content.text:
Good news: the third resume of the web accessibility run finally went clean — **104/104 agents, 0 errors, real synthesis.** Whatever caused the org access outage was transient, at least for this run. Committed and pushed.

**What it confirmed, and it's sharper than what I had:**

- **Grid vs. table is a keyboard-model decision, not a styling one.** A grid exposes exactly **one** focusable element to the page's tab sequence — arrows move inside it (roving tabindex). Every focusable element in a table stays in the tab sequence. Same visual table, two completely different keyboard experiences depending on which pattern gets picked.
- **Combobox forces a closed choice of exactly four popup roles** — listbox, tree, grid, or dialog — each carrying its own keyboard contract, plus `aria-expanded` that must mirror the visible open/closed state.
- **Menu/menubar's Tab key does the opposite of what you'd guess** — it *exits* the widget rather than navigating within it; arrows do the navigating.
- **The measured harm behind "no ARIA is better than bad ARIA"** — WebAIM Million 2026, ~1M pages: pages using ARIA average **59.1 detected errors vs. 42 without, ~41% more**, scaling with ARIA attribute count. Of pages using `role="menu"`, **22% actively introduce barriers** from incomplete markup. The APG's own framing: a role is just "a promise" — it carries zero native keyboard behavior on its own.

**Honest gap, stated by the run itself rather than papered over:** SPA route-change focus management and `aria-live`/live-region behavior returned **zero surviving claims across three attempts.** Marked unresearched, not absent — those still need the manual browser-verification treatment.

The other three runs (native mobile, native a11y+legal, tablet+desktop) made real further progress this pass — native a11y+legal's verify-stage count jumped to 81 — but none has sent a completion notification yet, so they're still in flight. I'll process each as it lands.

content.text:
Two of four now clean. This one **cross-validates** the Apple target-size table I pulled by hand earlier — three independent primary sources converge on the same 44×44pt/28×28pt figures I got from one page read, which is good confirmation the manual method wasn't a fluke.

**New depth beyond what I had:** Apple's Dynamic Type ramp is **12 sizes total** — 7 standard plus 5 accessibility (AX1–AX5). Body text scales 17pt → 53pt, roughly 3.1×, crossing 200% already at AX3. And the scaling is non-uniform across styles — at the top of the ramp, default-size Body (53pt) nearly *equals* default-size Headline. A layout can't just handle "bigger text"; it has to survive the hierarchy compressing.

**The cleanest native-vs-web gap in the whole project:** Apple explicitly **excludes system-level Zoom and Hover Text** from counting toward its 200% enlargement target — App Store Connect enforces this as a pass/fail bar. On the web, browser zoom satisfies WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10 by design. Same accessibility feature, opposite verdict depending on platform. A web-derived checklist would wrongly treat native OS zoom as sufficient.

Also confirmed: VoiceOver's `label` and `value` are separate channels — conflating them causes doubled speech like "checkbox, checkbox." And Android 14's font scaling is non-linear, confirmed from primary source — `4sp + 20sp ≠ 24sp`, which breaks naive additive layout math.

**Legal half (EAA, ADA Title II, Section 508, WCAG 2.2 binding status) is still a total blank** — zero surviving claims across every attempt on this topic specifically. Two runs down, two to go.

# Research — tablet + desktop, salvaged from a broken synthesis

**Date:** 2026-08-01
**Method:** deep-research harness, resumed three times. Final run: 107/107 agents, 0 hard
errors — but its **synthesis step returned a broken placeholder**, not real output.

---

## The bug, stated plainly

The final resume's result object was:

```json
"summary": "test",
"findings": [{"claim": "test claim", "confidence": "high",
              "sources": ["https://example.com"], "evidence": "test evidence"}]
```

That is not degraded content — it is a literal test stub that happened to satisfy the
output schema (every required field present, plausible-looking types) and so passed
validation without erroring. `agents_error: 0` because the harness never saw a failure;
it saw a well-formed object.

**This is worse than an error, because it doesn't announce itself as broken.** If I had
taken the notification at face value and written `DIRECTION.md` guidance sourced to
`example.com`, that would have shipped silently. The only reason it didn't is that every
research doc in this project gets read against its actual JSON before being written up —
the same discipline that already caught three fabricated quotes elsewhere in this session.

**What survived, because they are pass-through fields the synthesis LLM never touches:**
the `refuted` array (4 real claims, real votes, real URLs) and the `sources` bibliography
(21 real primary-source URLs with per-source claim counts). Those are written below.

**What did not survive in this run's output, but is real and recoverable:** the confirmed
claims. This run's *second* resume (before the synthesis bug) returned them directly in a
partial notification, which I read and still have. They are reproduced below, sourced the
same way every other doc in this project sources a claim.

---

## Confirmed claims, recovered from the pre-synthesis verification pass

### iPadOS multitasking is a first-class appearance state, on par with Dark Mode

> "Adapt seamlessly to appearance changes — like device orientation, multitasking modes,
> Dark Mode, and Dynamic Type — and transition effortlessly to running in macOS, letting
> people choose the configurations that work best for them."

Source: `developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/platforms/designing-for-ipados/`

An iPad app does not get to treat multitasking as an edge case checked once at the end.
It sits in the same category as orientation and dark mode — a first-class state the
design has to hold from the start.

### Hybrid input is the documented default, not an edge case

> "People can interact with iPad using Multi-Touch gestures and virtual keyboards, an
> attached keyboard or pointing device, Apple Pencil, or voice, and they often combine
> multiple input modes."

Same source. Confirms and sharpens the finding already in `tablet-desktop-verified.md` —
Apple states this as the *fundamental* device characteristic of iPadOS, not a
compatibility footnote.

### Large-display guidance: minimize modals and full-screen transitions

> "Take advantage of the large display to elevate the content people care about,
> minimizing modal interfaces and full-screen transitions, and positioning onscreen
> controls where they're easy to reach, but not in the way."

Same source. This is the opposite instinct from phone design, where a full-screen push is
the default pattern for anything secondary. On a large display, that reflex is named as
the thing to avoid.

### Windows resize continuously, macOS-style — confirming the Split View/Slide Over/Stage Manager absence

> "People can freely resize windows down to a minimum width and height, similar to window
> behavior in macOS. It's important to account for this resizing behavior and the full
> range of possible window sizes when designing your layout."

Source: `developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/layout`

This independently confirms the finding already written up in `tablet-desktop-verified.md`
from the manual browser pass — Split View, Slide Over, and Stage Manager as named modes are
gone from current guidance, replaced by continuous free resize. Two separate methods, same
conclusion.

### The collapse order: defer compact, hide tertiary columns first

> "As someone resizes a window, defer switching to a compact view for as long as possible.
> Design for a full-screen view first, and only switch to a compact view when a version of
> the full layout no longer fits... For more complex layouts such as [split views], prefer
> hiding tertiary columns such as inspectors as the view narrows."

Same source. Adds a specific detail the manual pass didn't reach: when a multi-column
layout has to shed a column under narrowing, the *tertiary* column (an inspector, not the
primary or secondary content) goes first.

### Size classes are binary, and iPad never varies on them

> "A size class is a value that's either regular or compact, where regular refers to a
> larger screen or a screen in landscape orientation and compact refers to a smaller
> screen or a screen in portrait orientation."

Same source, cross-checked against the device table: every current iPad model —
Pro 12.9", Pro 11", Pro 10.5", Air 13", Air 11", 11", 9.7", mini 7.9" — is **regular
width, regular height in both orientations.** iPhones vary by orientation; iPads do not.
This is the primary-source confirmation for the earlier finding that on iPadOS you design
against *available width*, not against size class, because the size class never changes as
a window resizes.

---

## Refuted — plausible claims the panel checked and could not support

Do not reuse these even though each sounds like something Apple would say.

- **"Apple explicitly directs designers to support combined-input interactions rather than
  designing for one input mode at a time."** Voted 0-3. The primary source states hybrid
  input is common, not that supporting simultaneous combination is a mandate.
- **"The pointing device is additive rather than substitutive — it does not replace touch —
  and an app must deliver an equivalent experience across gestures, pointer, and
  keyboard."** Voted 1-2, contested. `pointing-devices` HIG page doesn't state this as
  cleanly as the claim implies.
- **"Apple names the specific set of non-full-screen configurations an app must be tested
  in: full screen, Split View, Slide Over, Picture in Picture, and dynamic resizing under
  Stage Manager."** Voted 0-3. Checked against Apple's own `building-a-desktop-class-ipad-app`
  doc — even that page does not name Split View or Slide Over. Consistent with the
  earlier finding that this vocabulary is gone from current guidance, not just the
  Multitasking page.
- **"Designers should NOT build custom keyboard navigation for standard controls — Full
  Keyboard Access is the designated mechanism."** Voted 0-3. Not supported as stated; the
  real guidance is more scoped than this claim represents.

---

## Sources actually fetched (real, from this run)

Apple: `designing-for-ipados`, `layout`, `split-views`, `pointing-devices`,
`building-a-desktop-class-ipad-app`, `keyboards`, `the-menu-bar`, `windows`,
`designing-for-macos`, `drag-and-drop`

Google: `developer.android.com/develop/adaptive-apps/guides/use-window-size-classes`,
`m3.material.io/foundations/layout/applying-layout/window-size-classes`,
`developer.android.com/docs/quality-guidelines/adaptive-app-quality`,
`m3.material.io/components/navigation-rail/guidelines`,
`developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/layout/canonical-layouts`

Microsoft: `learn.microsoft.com` keyboard-accelerators, titlebar-design,
apply-snap-layout-menu, commanding-basics

Electron: `electronjs.org` custom-title-bar, api/menu

One source came back marked `"quality":"unreliable","claimCount":0` —
`m3.material.io/foundations/layout/canonical-layouts/overview` — so Material's canonical
layouts (list-detail, supporting pane, feed) named in the original research question were
**not actually verified** from that page. Still open.

---

## What is still genuinely open after four attempts at this topic

- Material's canonical layouts (list-detail, supporting pane, feed) — the source that
  should confirm these came back unreliable
- Windows/Fluent keyboard-shortcut divergence from macOS, in detail (sources were fetched,
  content not yet synthesized)
- Electron/Tauri's "website in a window" failure and the native-feel checklist (sources
  fetched, content not yet synthesized)
- Everything under desktop menu-bar and window-management specifics beyond what's quoted
  above

## Process note for future runs

If a `deep-research` synthesis result contains implausibly generic content (`"test"`,
round numbers, `example.com`), treat it as a harness bug and go straight to the journal
rather than trusting the top-level summary. This is now the second and third distinct
failure mode observed in this project, after the session-boundary process death and the
transient org-access outage — none of the three were survivable by trusting the tool's own
completion notification without inspecting the underlying data.

Honest answer: **no, we don't have everything — but we have everything that determines the architecture**, which is the part that's expensive to get wrong. Here's the real ledger:

**Solid, verified, ready to write from:**
WCAG 2.2's design-time criteria · Apple + Material target/type/contrast numbers (cross-validated twice) · Liquid Glass and M3 Expressive · Dynamic Type and the 12-size ramp · VoiceOver grouping · ARIA APG pattern commitments · WebAIM Million's measured ARIA harm · Material's five breakpoints · macOS window states · the Split View/Slide Over/Stage Manager deletion · DTCG token format.

**Still genuinely empty after every attempt:**

| Gap | Attempts | Why it's still open |
|---|---|---|
| Legal (EAA, ADA Title II, 508) | 3 runs, 0 claims | Never survived verification once |
| SPA focus mgmt + live regions | 3 runs, 0 claims | Same |
| Icons | never researched | No workflow ever covered it |
| `BREAKING.md` | never researched | — |
| i18n beyond RTL | never researched | — |
| Nav models, safe areas, gestures | 0 surviving | Cached claims exist, unverified |

**But three of those aren't really research problems**, which changes the plan:

- **`BREAKING.md` is authorship, not research.** Nobody publishes "when to violate design conventions" as a primary source. It gets written from the collision/subversion material already in `STYLES.md` plus judgment. Waiting on a research run for it would be waiting forever.
- **Icons and i18n** need one targeted browser pass each — SF Symbols/Material Symbols, and CLDR/text-expansion figures. That's a 10-minute job, not a 100-agent workflow.
- **Legal** needs one browser pass on EUR-Lex and ada.gov. The workflows kept failing on it because law sites resist summarizers, which is exactly the failure the browser fixes.

So the right move isn't another research phase. It's to **fold the research per-file, at the moment I write that file** — verify icons right before writing the icons section, not in the abstract. That's how the gaps close without a fourth round of workflow roulette.

Moving to the plan.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/taha/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.2.0/skills/writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
````

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# inter.face integrity checks. No deps beyond coreutils + jq.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
FAIL=0
fail() { printf '  FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAIL=1; }
ok()   { printf '  ok: %s\n' "$1"; }

echo "== placeholder scan =="
# The deep-research harness once returned a literal "test claim" / example.com
# stub that passed schema validation. Never let that reach a shipped file.
HITS=$(grep -rniE 'example\.com|\bTBD\b|\bTODO\b|Lorem ipsum|test claim|FIXME|XXX' \
  --include='*.md' --include='*.json' --include='*.mdc' . \
  2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\./docs/' | grep -v '^\./\.git' || true)
if [ -n "$HITS" ]; then fail "placeholder text in shipped files:"; echo "$HITS" | sed 's/^/    /'
else ok "no placeholders"; fi

echo "== resident budget =="
if [ -f AGENTS.md ]; then
  N=$(wc -l < AGENTS.md | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$N" -le 200 ] && ok "AGENTS.md ${N} lines (<=200)" || fail "AGENTS.md ${N} lines, budget 200"
else fail "AGENTS.md missing"; fi

echo "== json validity =="
for f in .claude-plugin/plugin.json .claude-plugin/marketplace.json \
         .codex-plugin/plugin.json gemini-extension.json opencode.json; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    jq empty "$f" 2>/dev/null && ok "$f parses" || fail "$f is not valid JSON"
  else fail "$f missing"; fi
done

echo "== skill frontmatter =="
for f in skills/inter.face/SKILL.md commands/interface.md .cursor/rules/inter.face.mdc; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    head -1 "$f" | grep -q '^---$' && ok "$f has frontmatter" || fail "$f missing opening ---"
  else fail "$f missing"; fi
done

echo "== internal links resolve =="
BROKEN=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  src=${line%%:*}; target=${line#*:}
  dir=$(dirname "$src")
  [ -e "$dir/$target" ] || { fail "broken link in $src -> $target"; BROKEN=1; }
done < <(grep -rhoE '\]\(\.{1,2}/[^)#]+\)' --include='*.md' . 2>/dev/null \
         | grep -v '^\./docs/' >/dev/null 2>&1; \
         grep -rnoE '\]\((\.{1,2}/[^)#]+)\)' --include='*.md' . 2>/dev/null \
         | grep -v '/docs/' | sed -E 's/^([^:]+):[0-9]+:\]\((.*)\)$/\1:\2/')
[ "$BROKEN" -eq 0 ] && ok "all relative links resolve"

echo "== every reference file forks on surface class =="
for f in STYLES.md CRAFT.md TOOLS.md SURFACES.md ACCESS.md; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    if grep -qiE 'page-shaped' "$f" && grep -qiE 'tool-shaped' "$f"; then
      ok "$f forks on surface class"
    else fail "$f does not address both page-shaped and tool-shaped"; fi
  fi
done

echo "== Apple numbers ship as pairs =="
if [ -f SURFACES.md ]; then
  if grep -q '44' SURFACES.md && grep -q '28' SURFACES.md; then
    ok "SURFACES.md carries default AND minimum"
  else fail "SURFACES.md must carry 44pt default AND 28pt minimum, never 44 alone"; fi
fi

echo
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] && echo "ALL CHECKS PASS" || echo "CHECKS FAILED"
exit "$FAIL"
```

**2. The four target numbers are four different things.**

| Standard | Number | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) | 24×24 CSS px effective area | web; satisfiable by size **or** the geometric spacing exception |
| Apple iOS/iPadOS | **44×44 pt default, 28×28 pt minimum** | native iOS controls |

Decision procedure: cross-platform-neutral takes **48dp / 44pt**, clearing every floor. A platform-committed design may use its own default. Nothing ships at a platform *minimum* without a stated reason — a minimum is for constrained cases, not a target.

Spacing is a separate obligation: Material 8dp between targets; Apple ~12pt padding around bezelled elements and ~**24pt** around bezel-less ones (double).

**3. Type and scaling.** Apple default/minimum per platform: iOS+iPadOS 17/11 · macOS 13/10 · tvOS 29/23 · visionOS 17/12 · watchOS 16/12. Dynamic Type is **12 sizes** (7 standard + AX1–AX5); Body runs 17pt → 53pt, ~3.1×, crossing 200% at AX3. Layout guidance: switch side-by-side to vertical stack, let text wrap rather than truncate. Android 14 max scaling 200% with a **non-linear curve — `4sp + 20sp ≠ 24sp`**, which breaks additive layout math.

**4. Liquid Glass.** Functional layer for controls and navigation only. **Never the content layer** — the one exception is transient controls (sliders, toggles) while active. Sparingly on custom controls. Two variants: regular (adaptive, for components carrying significant text — alerts, sidebars, popovers) and clear (only over visually rich media, with a **35% opacity dark dimming layer** if the underlying content is bright). Never mix the two variants; never stack glass on glass. Re-renders under Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast — both are designed states.

**Open with the structural claim**, because it is the reason this file exists:

In the three parent pipelines it was a Loop 8 checklist — and across ~5,000 lines they contained zero mentions of ARIA, focus management, live regions, or accessible names, while marking accessibility a hard rule. **WCAG 2.2's six new A/AA criteria as design decisions:**
- 2.5.8 target size — 24×24 CSS px effective area, satisfiable by size **or** the geometric spacing exception (a 24px circle centered on each undersized target must not intersect another). A token and layout decision.
- 2.5.7 dragging — a visible **non-drag pointer affordance** for every author-built drag. Keyboard support does *not* satisfy it; the affordance occupies layout space. Applies to reorder lists, kanban, map panning.
- 2.4.11 focus not obscured — sticky chrome geometry that never entirely covers a focused element.
- 3.3.8 accessible authentication — no cognitive function test; never block paste or password managers.
- 3.3.7 redundant entry, 3.2.6 consistent help.

State that **WCAG 2.2 AA is the operative target**: WCAG 3.0 is a Working Draft (3 March 2026) whose own text says it has "several years of work" left and does not deprecate WCAG 2.

**ARIA pattern choice is a design decision** (from `web-a11y-patterns.md`):
- **grid vs table** is a keyboard-model commitment: a grid exposes exactly **one** focusable element to the page tab sequence (roving tabindex); every focusable element in a table stays in the sequence. Same visual table, two different keyboard experiences.
- **combobox** forces a closed choice of four popup roles — listbox, tree, grid, dialog — each with its own keyboard contract, plus `aria-expanded` mirroring visible state.
- **menu/menubar**: Tab *exits* the widget; arrows navigate.
- **modal dialog** bundles focus trap + bidirectional focus transfer + content-dependent initial focus.
- **disclosure vs accordion** is a content-structure decision, not an implementation one. (Flag: this boundary is contested — a W3C issue is open with no editor resolution.)

**The measured case for restraint**, WebAIM Million 2026 (~1M home pages): pages using ARIA average **59.1 detected errors vs 42 without — ~41% more**, scaling with attribute count. Of pages using `role="menu"`, **22% actively introduce barriers** from incomplete markup. An ARIA role is, in the APG's words, "a promise" — it carries no native keyboard behavior. *No ARIA is better than bad ARIA.*

**Native accessibility, and where a web checklist misses:**
- Apple targets **200%** text enlargement (140% watchOS) and **explicitly excludes system Zoom and Hover Text** from counting toward it. Browser zoom *does* satisfy WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10. Same feature, opposite verdict by platform — this is the cleanest native-vs-web divergence found.
- **VoiceOver grouping is a layout-time decision.** Ungrouped, VoiceOver reads every image then every caption. Visual proximity encodes relationship silently for sighted users and not at all otherwise unless a designer declares it.
- **label and value are separate channels** — label names the field, value carries content. Conflating them causes doubled speech.
- Apple's contrast boundary is **17pt**, not the web's 18px/14pt-bold. A design system carrying one contrast rule across web and iOS uses the wrong breakpoint on one of them.
- Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast re-render Liquid Glass — designed states.

**i18n section** (folded in, not a separate file): `§13` covers script, direction, and never mangling a name. Add what the parents lacked — text expansion (German runs long; a layout tight at English width breaks), CJK line breaking, and that plural rules are not a two-case if-statement.
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# inter.face integrity checks. No deps beyond coreutils + jq.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
FAIL=0
fail() { printf '  FAIL: %s\n' "$1"; FAIL=1; }
ok()   { printf '  ok: %s\n' "$1"; }

echo "== placeholder scan =="
# The deep-research harness once returned a literal "test claim" / example.com
# stub that passed schema validation. Never let that reach a shipped file.
HITS=$(grep -rniE 'example\.com|\bTBD\b|\bTODO\b|Lorem ipsum|test claim|FIXME|XXX' \
  --include='*.md' --include='*.json' --include='*.mdc' . \
  2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\./docs/' | grep -v '^\./\.git' || true)
if [ -n "$HITS" ]; then fail "placeholder text in shipped files:"; echo "$HITS" | sed 's/^/    /'
else ok "no placeholders"; fi

echo "== resident budget =="
if [ -f AGENTS.md ]; then
  N=$(wc -l < AGENTS.md | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$N" -le 200 ] && ok "AGENTS.md ${N} lines (<=200)" || fail "AGENTS.md ${N} lines, budget 200"
else fail "AGENTS.md missing"; fi

echo "== json validity =="
for f in .claude-plugin/plugin.json .claude-plugin/marketplace.json \
         .codex-plugin/plugin.json gemini-extension.json opencode.json; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    jq empty "$f" 2>/dev/null && ok "$f parses" || fail "$f is not valid JSON"
  else fail "$f missing"; fi
done

echo "== skill frontmatter =="
for f in skills/inter.face/SKILL.md commands/interface.md .cursor/rules/inter.face.mdc; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    head -1 "$f" | grep -q '^---$' && ok "$f has frontmatter" || fail "$f missing opening ---"
  else fail "$f missing"; fi
done

echo "== internal links resolve =="
BROKEN=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  src=${line%%:*}; target=${line#*:}
  dir=$(dirname "$src")
  [ -e "$dir/$target" ] || { fail "broken link in $src -> $target"; BROKEN=1; }
done < <(grep -rhoE '\]\(\.{1,2}/[^)#]+\)' --include='*.md' . 2>/dev/null \
         | grep -v '^\./docs/' >/dev/null 2>&1; \
         grep -rnoE '\]\((\.{1,2}/[^)#]+)\)' --include='*.md' . 2>/dev/null \
         | grep -v '/docs/' | sed -E 's/^([^:]+):[0-9]+:\]\((.*)\)$/\1:\2/')
[ "$BROKEN" -eq 0 ] && ok "all relative links resolve"

echo "== every reference file forks on surface class =="
for f in STYLES.md CRAFT.md TOOLS.md SURFACES.md ACCESS.md; do
  if [ -f "$f" ]; then
    if grep -qiE 'page-shaped' "$f" && grep -qiE 'tool-shaped' "$f"; then
      ok "$f forks on surface class"
    else fail "$f does not address both page-shaped and tool-shaped"; fi
  fi
done

echo "== Apple numbers ship as pairs =="
if [ -f SURFACES.md ]; then
  if grep -q '44' SURFACES.md && grep -q '28' SURFACES.md; then
    ok "SURFACES.md carries default AND minimum"
  else fail "SURFACES.md must carry 44pt default AND 28pt minimum, never 44 alone"; fi
fi

echo
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ] && echo "ALL CHECKS PASS" || echo "CHECKS FAILED"
exit "$FAIL"
```

**Open with the structural claim**, because it is the reason this file exists:

In the three parent pipelines it was a Loop 8 checklist — and across ~5,000 lines they contained zero mentions of ARIA, focus management, live regions, or accessible names, while marking accessibility a hard rule. **WCAG 2.2's six new A/AA criteria as design decisions:**
- 2.5.8 target size — 24×24 CSS px effective area, satisfiable by size **or** the geometric spacing exception (a 24px circle centered on each undersized target must not intersect another). A token and layout decision.
- 2.5.7 dragging — a visible **non-drag pointer affordance** for every author-built drag. Keyboard support does *not* satisfy it; the affordance occupies layout space. Applies to reorder lists, kanban, map panning.
- 2.4.11 focus not obscured — sticky chrome geometry that never entirely covers a focused element.
- 3.3.8 accessible authentication — no cognitive function test; never block paste or password managers.
- 3.3.7 redundant entry, 3.2.6 consistent help.

State that **WCAG 2.2 AA is the operative target**: WCAG 3.0 is a Working Draft (3 March 2026) whose own text says it has "several years of work" left and does not deprecate WCAG 2.

**ARIA pattern choice is a design decision** (from `web-a11y-patterns.md`):
- **grid vs table** is a keyboard-model commitment: a grid exposes exactly **one** focusable element to the page tab sequence (roving tabindex); every focusable element in a table stays in the sequence. Same visual table, two different keyboard experiences.
- **combobox** forces a closed choice of four popup roles — listbox, tree, grid, dialog — each with its own keyboard contract, plus `aria-expanded` mirroring visible state.
- **menu/menubar**: Tab *exits* the widget; arrows navigate.
- **modal dialog** bundles focus trap + bidirectional focus transfer + content-dependent initial focus.
- **disclosure vs accordion** is a content-structure decision, not an implementation one. (Flag: this boundary is contested — a W3C issue is open with no editor resolution.)

**The measured case for restraint**, WebAIM Million 2026 (~1M home pages): pages using ARIA average **59.1 detected errors vs 42 without — ~41% more**, scaling with attribute count. Of pages using `role="menu"`, **22% actively introduce barriers** from incomplete markup. An ARIA role is, in the APG's words, "a promise" — it carries no native keyboard behavior. *No ARIA is better than bad ARIA.*

**Native accessibility, and where a web checklist misses:**
- Apple targets **200%** text enlargement (140% watchOS) and **explicitly excludes system Zoom and Hover Text** from counting toward it. Browser zoom *does* satisfy WCAG 1.4.4/1.4.10. Same feature, opposite verdict by platform — this is the cleanest native-vs-web divergence found.
- **VoiceOver grouping is a layout-time decision.** Ungrouped, VoiceOver reads every image then every caption. Visual proximity encodes relationship silently for sighted users and not at all otherwise unless a designer declares it.
- **label and value are separate channels** — label names the field, value carries content. Conflating them causes doubled speech.
- Apple's contrast boundary is **17pt**, not the web's 18px/14pt-bold. A design system carrying one contrast rule across web and iOS uses the wrong breakpoint on one of them.
- Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast re-render Liquid Glass — designed states.

# Subagent-Driven Development

Execute plan by dispatching a fresh implementer subagent per task, a task review (spec compliance + code quality) after each, and a broad whole-branch review at the end.

**Why subagents:** You delegate tasks to specialized agents with isolated context. By precisely crafting their instructions and context, you ensure they stay focused and succeed at their task. They should never inherit your session's context or history — you construct exactly what they need. This also preserves your own context for coordination work.

**Core principle:** Fresh subagent per task + task review (spec + quality) + broad final review = high quality, fast iteration

**Narration:** between tool calls, narrate at most one short line — the
ledger and the tool results carry the record.

**Continuous execution:** Do not pause to check in with your human partner between tasks. Execute all tasks from the plan without stopping. The only reasons to stop are: BLOCKED status you cannot resolve, ambiguity that genuinely prevents progress, or all tasks complete. "Should I continue?" prompts and progress summaries waste their time — they asked you to execute the plan, so execute it.

## When to Use

```dot

    "Have implementation plan?" [shape=diamond];
    "Tasks mostly independent?" [shape=diamond];
    "Stay in this session?" [shape=diamond];

    "Stay in this session?" -> "executing-plans" [label="no - parallel session"];
}
```

**vs. Executing Plans (parallel session):**
- Same session (no context switch)
- Fresh subagent per task (no context pollution)
- Review after each task (spec compliance + code quality), broad review at the end
- Faster iteration (no human-in-loop between tasks)
